title: REA: Reverse Engineer Anything
description: REA is an MIT-licensed MCP server and CLI that connects coding agents to locally run tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript/Electron applications, .NET assemblies, websites, Android artifacts, firmware, and runtime behavior. It returns findings with supporting evidence and limitations, and the same workflows are available from a terminal.
capabilityNote: Setup registers REA with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, and other agents. Support for a target can require Hopper, Ghidra, IDA, JADX, a browser, or other host tools, and REA requires specified Node.js versions.

title: Laya
description: Laya is an open-source non-autoregressive decision engine that answers typed classification, scoring, and boolean questions over text states in a single forward pass without generating text. It uses encoder checkpoints (ModernBERT and mmBERT) trained with reinforcement learning via strictly proper scoring rules (RLCD) to provide fast, hallucination-free routing and triage.
capabilityNote: Executes typed decisions in approximately 33 ms per single question (7.2 ms batched on a T4 GPU) across 100+ languages, supporting context lengths up to 8,192 tokens.

sources.title: GitHub - NandhaKishorM/laya: Multilingual, non-autoregressive System 1 decision engine

title: Beam (Reflection AI)
description: Reflection AI's first open-weight model: a text-only sparse mixture-of-experts with 501B total and 23B active parameters, a 1M-token context window and Apache 2.0 weights on Hugging Face in BF16, FP8 and NVFP4. It targets coding, reasoning and agentic work.
capabilityNote: All benchmark and efficiency figures are Reflection's own. The post says Beam is comparable to GLM-5.2 with 3-4x less inference compute (an estimate that excludes prefill and serving), and concedes Kimi K3 still leads on raw capability.

title: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL
description: NVIDIA's open-weight vision-language model: a Mamba-2/Transformer hybrid mixture-of-experts with 120B total and 12B active parameters, text, image and video input, text output, up to 1M tokens of context and native multi-token prediction. Weights ship under the OpenMDW-1.1 licence.
capabilityNote: NVIDIA's own table shows it behind several rivals on agentic coding (Terminal-Bench 2.1 60.67 against up to 85.80 for others in the same table). The model card lists 4x H100 or 2x GB200 for BF16 serving.

title: Gemini 4 Carbon
description: Google's cybersecurity-focused frontier model, released two weeks after Gemini 4 Argon. Access starts with a subset of cyber defenders and widens to trusted partners through the Fairwind Program; developer and consumer availability is promised later.
capabilityNote: Every figure is Google's own: 59 and first place on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0, 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro, 54.8% on ExploitGym, 71.0% on CWE-bench. Google says it is joining the US government's voluntary pre-release testing. Not generally available at announcement.

title: Genie 4
description: DeepMind's real-time interactive world model, with native generated audio. Users change weather, camera and objects by text while the simulation runs, and Gemini provides the reasoning that keeps scenes coherent. DeepMind names robotics simulation and agent training (SIMA) as uses.
capabilityNote: A research preview for trusted testers; Google AI Ultra and Gemini API early-access partners are "coming soon". Google's own limits: details and object permanence drift, sessions last a few minutes, and text is rarely legible. The page gives no date, so 27 October comes from press coverage.

title: Anthropic files for an IPO
description: Anthropic, PBC filed a Form S-1 with the SEC for an initial public offering of Class A common stock, planned for the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT.
capabilityNote: The registration statement was not yet effective as of the 10 November roadshow launch, and Anthropic's announcements give no financials; press figures conflict, so none are used here.

majorUpdates.title: Roadshow launched
majorUpdates.summary: Anthropic proposed 825,000,000 Class A shares at an expected $70.00-$78.00, applying to list on Nasdaq as ANT. The registration statement was still not effective.

sources.title: Anthropic: files S-1 with the SEC for proposed IPO

title: GPT-6.1 Terra
description: OpenAI's fast, cheaper model for computer use and everyday work tasks. Standard API prices are 50% below GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol: $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output. It is available to Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex, and in the API as gpt-6.1-terra.
capabilityNote: All figures are OpenAI's own. At max reasoning it solves 50.3% of Terminal-Bench 4.0 tasks (GPT-5.6 Terra: 21.5%), and OpenAI says it matches GPT-6 Astra on Agents' Last Exam at one-tenth the per-token price. It meets the Critical cybersecurity threshold under OpenAI's Preparedness Framework. OpenAI says Sol and Astra remain better for the hardest coding tasks.

title: Kimi K3.1 Pro
description: Moonshot's post-trained upgrade of Kimi K3: an open-weight, natively multimodal model with 2.8T total and 104B active parameters and a 1M-token context window, plus a Highspeed API variant that Moonshot says is 2-3x faster. Weights are on Hugging Face under the Kimi K3.1 Pro licence; it is also live on Kimi.ai, Kimi Work, Kimi Code and the API.
capabilityNote: The licence is a custom MIT-style one: free to use, modify and sell, but a Model-as-a-Service business earning over $20M in any 12 months needs a separate agreement with Moonshot, and products above 100M monthly users or $20M monthly revenue must display "Kimi K3.1-Pro". Internal use is exempt. All benchmark figures are Moonshot's own: Terminal-Bench 4.0 65.7% (GPT-6 Astra 58.2%, Claude Opus 5.5 66.4%). Moonshot says it removed cyber-related data from training to limit misuse.

sources.title: moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro on Hugging Face (model card, licence)

title: Claude Duet
description: A separate Anthropic app where Claude works as a proactive agent: it sends a morning brief, takes tasks by message, works on its own cloud computer with connected apps, and asks for approval before acting on your behalf. Anthropic says it is powered by Opus 5.5.
capabilityNote: A research preview on a waitlist for US Pro, Max and Ultra subscribers; Team and Enterprise are not included. Anthropic warns it may misread a thread, miscalibrate urgency or miss something that arrives between check-ins.

title: ChatGPT Wallet
description: OpenAI's payments product for agents, delivered through dots. The agent pays with a payment-network token instead of the user's real card details, and every purchase needs a security check such as Face ID. It was built with American Express, Mastercard and Visa and keeps card rewards and dispute protections for eligible disputes.
capabilityNote: Limited availability: ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US at first. OpenAI warns some sites may block agent purchases and published a Commerce Partner Playbook for businesses. The "1.2B people use ChatGPT each week" figure is OpenAI's own.

title: GPT-6 Cyber
description: OpenAI's cybersecurity-specialised model, offered through Daybreak: Daybreak Blue for verified defenders and Daybreak Red for exploit development and authorised testing. OpenAI classifies it as Critical in cybersecurity under its Preparedness Framework, up from High for GPT-5.6 Cyber.
capabilityNote: All figures are OpenAI's own: ExploitGym 48.5% (GPT-5.6 Cyber 32.1%), 99.93% out-of-scope avoidance without a deployment prompt, 948 Linux privilege-escalation exploits and 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox vulnerabilities. Access is restricted rather than general.

title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
description: Anthropic's upgrade of its top model tier. Fable and Mythos are the same underlying model: Fable has cyber and biology safeguards and is open to all users, while Mythos goes to verified cyber and life-sciences programmes. Fable 5.2 costs $8 per million input and $40 per million output tokens, with an optional fast mode at $16/$80.
capabilityNote: Anthropic's own claims: FrontierCode 2.0 49.1% (Opus 5.5 45.5%, GPT-6 Astra 42.8%, Gemini 4 Carbon 41.1%), up to 30% faster than 5.1, and a Fermat's Last Theorem formalisation in 30 hours during prerelease testing. Anthropic still recommends Opus 5.5 as the daily driver.

title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen
description: Google's fast, efficient Gemini 4 tier, priced at $1.50 per million input and $7.50 per million output tokens, flat across a 1M-token context. It brings Gemini 4 to every tier of AI Studio, the Gemini API, the Gemini app and Search, and ships with Orchestrator in Antigravity, which switches between Carbon and Hydrogen within one session.
capabilityNote: Google's own figures: Artificial Analysis index 51 at default high thinking (Argon 50), 54 at xhigh; Terminal-Bench 4.1 57% against 18.2% for Gemini 3.8 Flash; Orchestrator reached near-Carbon success on Terminal-Bench 4.0 with 24% less quota and 19% faster.

title: Muse Ember
description: Meta's smallest and cheapest Muse model, built for work agents repeat: tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction and long-document parsing. It is on the Meta Model API at $0.10 per million input and $0.50 per million output tokens.
capabilityNote: Meta's claims rest on Artificial Analysis runs plus a Meta-built composite: it matches Haiku 5.5's best score at about a third of the cost, with Terminal-Bench 4.0 40.9% (Haiku 5.5 39.2%) and Agents' Last Exam 61.6 (57.0). It trails Haiku 5.5 on FrontierCode 2.0 (27.2 vs 34.9). The Personal Superintelligence Index is Meta's own, and the cost figures use proposed pricing.

title: Inkling 2 Small
description: Thinking Machines Lab's second-generation model: a mixture-of-experts with 594B total and 17B active parameters, image input and variable effort. It launched on the Tinker platform with closed weights; Apache 2.0 weights followed on Hugging Face on 12 November after external safety testing.
capabilityNote: Its Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score is 31, an improvement on the lab's earlier models rather than a lead over frontier models. The lab reports FrontierCode v2.0 25.4%, second-highest in its comparison row. It is available through NVIDIA, Fireworks, Together, Baseten, Nebius, Modal and Cloudflare, and runs on vLLM, SGLang and Unsloth.

title: ScaleDown Constrained Decoding Models
description: Task-specific models from ScaleDown that each do one job: Classify scores user-defined labels, Extract pulls schema fields out of text, images or documents, and Summarize condenses long inputs. They accept up to 1M tokens and, ScaleDown says, skip token-by-token generation. Compress is an older separate model.
capabilityNote: The headline claims of 200x faster, 467x cheaper and SOTA accuracy are ScaleDown's own and come with no published method; one independent write-up reports ScaleDown's own benchmark page shows 2.2-13.9x faster, and a hands-on test found billed input tokens above the raw prompt, so short classifications cost about twice gpt-5-nano. "Constrained decoding" is also an existing technique. Summarize is described as abstractive, which is generation.

sources.title: Blog comparison of LLMs, Jev and CDMs (third-party)

title: Weight-Space Programming
creators: Takehi, Teoh, Zhang and Khattab (MIT CSAIL, per Snowflake's write-up)
description: A concept and early results showing that a frontier LLM can read and write a neural network's weights directly, without gradient descent: GPT-6 Astra identified what a small network was trained for from raw weights, and edited 0.016% of Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights, lifting MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1%.
capabilityNote: The 48.1% and the 0%-to-100% game-control fix are the authors' own early results. An independent follow-up (arXiv 2611.09382) on Qwen3.5-0.8B and 9B found gains of up to 29.45 points on MATH-500 from 1,023 changed parameters, but uneven transfer, and six of 16 editing trajectories kept the original weights because candidate edits could not be validated.

sources.title: Exploring Weight-Space Programming: Capabilities, Generalization, and Limitations (arXiv 2611.09382)
